title: The Seven Questions of the Persian Ambassador (TE)
summary: A Persian diplomat arrives with seven intricate diplomatic riddles. Birbal answers all seven in a single sentence.
full_text:
A grand ambassador from the court of Shah Abbas of Persia arrived in Agra, bringing gifts of silk carpets, turquoise chalices, and a sealed scroll containing seven delicate diplomatic questions. Standing before Emperor Akbar, the ambassador announced:

'Greetings to the Great Mughal. My sovereign has sent seven questions of philosophy and governance. If your counselors can answer them all without debate or delay, our kingdoms shall seal an everlasting trade treaty.'

The questions were read aloud:

'What is the brightest fire? What is the coldest wind? What is the deepest ocean? What is the swiftest horse? What is the strongest fortress? What is the sweetest fruit? And what is the most terrible weapon?'

The courtiers began whispering arguments about desert fires, Himalayan gales, and iron arrows.

Birbal stepped forward, bowed politely to the Persian ambassador, and answered with quiet eloquence:

'Excellency, the seven answers are known to every discerning soul:

'The brightest fire is the light of Truth, which banishes the darkest ignorance.

'The coldest wind is the breath of Envy, which freezes charity and friendship.

'The deepest ocean is the Human Heart, whose depths of desire and grief no lead line can fathom.

'The swiftest horse is Human Thought, which leaps across continents and stars in a fraction of an instant.

'The strongest fortress is a Ruler's Justice, which protects an empire better than walls of solid granite.

'The sweetest fruit is the Word of Kindness, which heals wounds and gladdens the weary spirit.

'And the most terrible weapon is a Treacherous Tongue, which slays reputations and ignites wars without drawing a drop of blood.'

The Persian ambassador stood in silent awe, then bowed low with folded hands: 'Emperor Akbar, your minister has answered seven volumes of philosophy with seven pearls of pure wisdom!'

Akbar embraced Birbal, and the diplomatic treaty was signed with rejoicing.
